findings.can_model_run_cpu_only: Partially YES. The .trt TensorRT engines CANNOT run on CPU at all (TensorRT requires an NVIDIA GPU). However Cell 2 ships a complete ONNX Runtime fallback path that explicitly supports CPUExecutionProvider, and the fp32 2x ONNX model exists (Dropbox link). So CPU-only inference is technically possible via onnxruntime + the ONNX weight only (2x, FP32).
findings.encoders_blocker: Cell 2's x264/x265 paths use h264_nvenc / hevc_nvenc - NVIDIA hardware encoders that hard-fail on a CPU-only runner. ProRes (prores_ks) and FFV1 are CPU encoders and would work. A GitHub Actions version would need the encoder mapped to libx264/libx265 (or ProRes/FFV1) - a small code change but mandatory.
findings.runner_limits: GitHub-hosted Linux runner: 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, ~14 GB SSD, 6-hour max job runtime, 2 GB artifact/file limits on releases. The 24-channel tiled CNN at 576x672 tiles on 4 CPU cores would plausibly take tens of seconds to minutes PER FRAME - a 10s 24fps clip (240 frames, 3 first-frame passes + temporal) could exceed the 6h job limit. Input must also be tiny (1080p pre-resize helps but 2x output of 1080p = 4K frames in RAM).
findings.feasibility_verdict: Technically feasible for very short/small test clips (proof-of-pipeline), NOT practical for real videos. Complexity: moderate (rewrite setup cell for CPU-only pip, swap NVENC->libx264/libx265, download ONNX from the Release, upload result as workflow artifact). Recommendation: keep Colab GPU as the product; Actions version only as a demo/smoke-test.

fix2_startup_speed.root_cause_confirmed: Compared original Cell 1 V15.5 vs current Cell A step by step. Differences adding time: (1) Original restored a warm pip cache (HF dataset legend2008/kzm-cache-v4, ~hundreds of MB, 8-way parallel snapshot_download) and ran every pip install with --cache-dir pointing at it; the rebuild used plain pip with an empty cache. Biggest single cost: pycuda has NO wheels on PyPI, so a cold 'pip install pycuda' compiles C++ against the CUDA toolkit (~2-4 min) while the warm cache held the pre-built wheel (~seconds). (2) The rebuild ran ~7 separate pip invocations, each paying full dependency-resolution overhead; original resolved within one cached session. (3) The rebuild unconditionally uninstalled+reinstalled tensorrt (tensorrt-cu12-libs wheel is ~2 GB) even when a compatible TensorRT was already importable. (4) The 5 weight files (~388 MB total) downloaded strictly sequentially via curl; original Cell 1 also did these sequentially, so this is unchanged-but-improvable, not a regression.
fix2_startup_speed.wheelhouse_alternative_assessed_and_reje: Hosting our own prebuilt pip wheel bundle as a GitHub Release asset (the direct equivalent of the HF cache) was assessed and rejected for two hard reasons: tensorrt-cu12-libs alone (~2.3 GB) exceeds GitHub's 2 GB per-Release-asset limit, and a prebuilt pycuda wheel is coupled to Colab's exact Python + CUDA toolkit versions, which cannot be built reliably without the live runtime (and would silently break when Colab upgrades its image). Documented as a deliberate decision.
replacement: Install-once detection: every dependency is import-probed first; only missing/wrong-version packages are installed, in ONE combined pip call (one resolution pass, pip output streams live).
TensorRT is kept if already importable at 10.x (turns re-runs in the same runtime from a ~2 GB reinstall into seconds).
Weight downloads now run 5-way parallel (ThreadPoolExecutor) from the GitHub Release CDN, with an aggregate tqdm bar showing real MB/%.
proteus_core.py is now always fetched fresh (tiny file; removes stale-core risk from the old 'skip if exists' logic).
Kept --prefer-binary everywhere so pip never attempts avoidable source builds.
fix2_startup_speed.expected_effect: First run: saves pip resolution overhead and parallelizes the ~388 MB weight fetch (~2-4x faster download step on Colab's link); pycuda source compile on first run is the one unavoidable cost without a credential-free prebuilt wheel. Re-runs in the same runtime: near-instant dependency step (all probes hit), weights skipped if already local.

fix3_tensorrt_invalid_context.diagnosis: Two layered causes. (a) Code/ordering bug: TensorRT 10.x implicit device context is thread-local; the Gradio worker thread that loads/executes the engine had no current CUDA context -> 'explicit_context_dependent failed: invalid device context - no currently active context'. (b) Portability risk: the .trt engines are compiled for one specific GPU arch/driver/TensorRT build, while Colab assigns T4/L4/A100 across sessions, so a static .trt can also be genuinely incompatible.
fix3_tensorrt_invalid_context.fix: proteus_core.py now initializes pycuda and makes a CUDA context current on the inference thread BEFORE any TensorRT deserialize/execute call, AND smoke-tests the TRT engine on the actual session GPU at model-load time; any failure auto-falls-back to the portable ONNX model via ONNX Runtime (CUDAExecutionProvider -> CPUExecutionProvider). GPU is detected at runtime; no manual user choice. Verified statically: ctx make/push (context); TRT deserialize; ONNX InferenceSession; auto TRT->ONNX fallback; GPU runtime detection

diagnosis_vs_original_cell1.root_cause_1_single_combined_pip_pass: update_2 merged ALL missing packages into ONE pip call (tensorrt-cu12 + tensorrt + pycuda + onnxruntime-gpu + onnxruntime + gradio + pillow + requests + tqdm). A single combined resolution forces pip's resolver to backtrack across tensorrt<11 / gradio / onnxruntime version constraints, re-downloading candidate wheels for tens of minutes. The original Cell 1 installed in SMALL ORDERED CALLS (numpy; tensorrt-cu12; tensorrt; pycuda; cv2), each resolving in seconds against the warm cache.
diagnosis_vs_original_cell1.root_cause_2_silent_pycuda_source_build: pycuda has no PyPI wheels. The warm cache's prebuilt pycuda wheel is CPython-version-specific; when it does not match Colab's current Python, pip compiles pycuda from source (nvcc/gcc, minutes) while showing only a 'Building wheel for pycuda' spinner line — indistinguishable from a hang.
diagnosis_vs_original_cell1.root_cause_3_onnxruntime_double_install: Cell A installed 'onnxruntime-gpu' AND 'onnxruntime' in the same pass; both packages own the same module directory, adding resolver churn and risking a broken install. Original Cell 2 ships onnxruntime-gpu only.

update_6.summary: User report: 2-pass presets (V2/V3) crash at Pass 2 'Engine warmup' with TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'NoneType', right after Pass 2 logs frames=None for the Pass 1 intermediate .mkv.

chain: 1) get_media_info() reads the frame count ONLY from ffprobe's stream nb_frames field.

2) The Pass 1 intermediate is FFV1 16-bit lossless in a Matroska (.mkv) container. Matroska stores NO per-stream frame count, so nb_frames comes back empty and get_media_info returned tf=None for Pass 2's input. Original uploads (mp4 etc.) DO store nb_frames, which is why Pass 1 always showed a real count and Pass 2 alone printed frames=None.
3) The processing loop backfills tf once decoding starts (if tf is None or fi > tf: tf = fi), so after frame 1 tf becomes the int 1.
4) The tqdm progress bar, however, was created BEFORE the loop with total=tf while tf was still None, so _pbar.total stayed None.

5) The guard 'if tf and fi > _pbar.total:' then passed (tf=1 truthy) and evaluated '1 > None' -> TypeError. It fires after frame 1 is processed; the per-frame message goes to the progress bar (not the log box), so the visible log shows the crash immediately after 'Engine warmup...' — matching the report exactly.
root_cause.why_only_pass2: Pass 1's input is the original upload (mp4/mov etc. with a stored nb_frames), so tf was an int and _pbar.total was never None. Pass 2 is the only path whose input is the pipeline's own FFV1/MKV intermediate — the one container family with no stored frame count.
root_cause.exact_crash_line: proteus_core.py process_video_pass: 'if tf and fi > _pbar.total:' with _pbar.total=None

update_6.was_pass2_tested_before: No. BUILD_STATE step5 verification was 'dependency resolution, notebook JSON validity, syntax compile, Gradio smoke-test, weight URL checks' only — no GPU/Colab here, and NO prior pass ever ran process_video_pass against a real Pass 1 FFV1 .mkv intermediate. The original Proteus Cell 2 read frames via OpenCV CAP_PROP_FRAME_COUNT (which counts/estimates for mkv), so the bug was introduced by the MotionSalt refactor to ffprobe nb_frames and went unnoticed because only original-upload inputs were ever exercised.
fix: get_media_info: ffprobe now also requests stream/format duration. When nb_frames is absent (tf would be None) it estimates tf = round(container_duration x fps) and logs that it did so. Matroska stores a reliable segment duration, and the processing loop already self-corrects tf if an estimate is off (if tf is None or fi > tf: tf = fi). A full ffprobe -count_frames scan was deliberately NOT used: it decodes the entire 16-bit FFV1 intermediate (minutes of I/O) just to fill a progress-bar total.

process_video_pass loop: the bar-total guard now reads 'if _pbar.total is None or (tf and fi > _pbar.total): _pbar.total = tf if tf else fi' — it keys off _pbar.total itself, so fi can never be compared against None again even if a future container yields neither nb_frames nor duration.

If neither nb_frames nor duration is available, tf stays None, a WARNING is logged, and the pipeline continues with an indeterminate progress bar instead of crashing (message construction is already None-safe; only the bar guard was not).
